item.title: Ghost Recon Wildlands: Operation Watchman Walkthrough
item.description:
Operation Watchman is one of the most frustrating missions in Ghost Recon Wildlands . Apart from having a mandatory no-kill stealth section, it will have players fighting back an endless wave of Unidad soldiers, which includes heavy infantry and helicopters. Failing any part of Operation Watchman in Ghost Recon Wildlands will force you to replay the entire thing from the start, so if you don't want to deal with that, here are some things you can try to make this mission go more smoothly.

What is Security Destabilization in Ghost Recon Wildlands?

Destabilization measures how much damage you've done to Santa Blanca in Ghost Recon Wildlands, and it determines the ending you get too.

By Marc Santos

Ghost Recon Wildlands: Operation Watchman Stealth Guide

You can only do Operation Watchman between 21:00 and 04:00 . Failing and restarting the mission will not freeze or reset the world time, so you'll have to reset the time of day manually if you ever take too long.

The first thing you need to do is infiltrate FOB Vibora without getting spotted or dropping any of the Unidad troops stationed there. Before you go, I strongly recommend bringing the following:

  • Diversion Lures
  • Proximity Mines
  • Diversion, Mortar, and Guns-for-Hire Rebel Support Skills
  • Anti-vehicle weapons like the HTI sniper rifle or underbarrel grenade launcher

Enter through the front gate, and use Diversion Lures to lure away the guards at the checkpoint and the base entrance . Then, hug the left side, vault over the sandbags in the small camp up the hill, then make your way to the left side of the FOB's main building. From here, be mindful of the following guard spawns/locations:

  1. One at the main entrance
  2. Snipers in the watch towers
  3. Guards inside the mess halls/armories to the left of the main building
  4. At least three guards patrolling the perimeter of the main building
  5. Sometimes, there are guards in the back room of the main building

Enter the main building through the back door, then head up the stairs. Speak with Sam Fisher, and get ready for the hardest part of this mission.

You can skip the stealth segment by flying a helicopter through the base's airspace and jumping before it gets shot down. If you keep getting spotted while parachuting down, you can instead clear the base a few in-game hours before the mission begins .

Operation Watchman: Surviving the Unidad Assault

After you speak with Sam, the entire Unidad base will go on alert, and you'll have to hold out until Sam's hack attempt is finished . If you're playing with AI teammates, they'll likely go down as soon as the fighting starts, so make sure you're ready to fight alone. I recommend bringing an M4A1 or another good CQB weapon to pair with your anti-vehicle weapon of choice.

When the bullets start flying and enemies come swarming, place your Proximity Mines on the doorways, and when one of them pops, put down another . This way, you'll only need to worry about enemies coming from the windows and the stairs.

Next, call-in all of your Rebel Support skills . Let the rebels fight Unidad soldiers outside so you can focus on the ones storming the building.

In my playthrough, I hugged the table next to the stairs and just waited for Unidad to pour in from the stairs and the window . Make sure to pick off the snipers from the watch towers too. At this point, it's all a matter of trying not to die while Sam does his business.

Never get caught with your pants down. Reload often, and if you have the grenade launcher attachment, prioritize using that to destroy helicopters instead of swapping to a different gun.

Extract with Sam

When Sam's done hacking, you'll have to somehow escape the FOB. If you hide for long enough, the Unidad alert level will eventually die out , giving you the opportunity to slip away. However, the road leading to the extraction point will have Unidad troops guarding certain checkpoints. You can drive past them, but it might be a little risky. Do your best to avoid them, or drive off-road.

Once you reach the hideout, a cutscene will play, and Operation Watchman will come to a close. You'll get a bunch of XP for your efforts, and not much else.

If you parked a helicopter near the FOB before starting the mission, you can use that to make your escape.

8 /10

Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands

item.title: To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown Quest Guide In Genshin Impact
item.description:
To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown is the first quest in the On One Side a Palace, On the Other a Tomb questline in Genshin Impact . You trigger it right after completing the In the Dwelling of Life series. In this quest, you will visit the Tsar’s tomb to obtain the Eye of Graeae’s final fragment piece.

A Great Heart Fettered by Slender Chains Quest Guide In Genshin Impact

Break four chains to free the giant Snegovik and complete the A Great Heart Fettered by Slender Chains quest in Genshin Impact.

By Nahda Nabiilah

To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown Quest In Genshin Impact

Here are the steps to completing the To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown quest in Genshin Impact :

  • Talk to the Eye of Graeae
  • Go to the place that the Eye of Graeae showed you
  • Find a path into the mountains
  • Advance into the snowstorm
  • Find the mechanism for the "hidden tracks"
  • Summon the "hidden tracks"
  • Board the train
  • Investigate the strange space
  • Investigate the next room
  • Read the notes sealed in Prime Ice
  • Find the source of the cat cries
  • Find a way out of the room
  • Leave
  • Try opening the door in front of the staircase
  • Go to the second floor and search
  • Head to the snow-covered palace

Talk to the Eye of Graeae

Talk to the Eye of Graeae by heading to the Central Station, then find the train carriage he's inside.

Once you've arrived at the Snowgrave area, continue following the quest marker until you need to find a path into the mountains.

Find a Path Into the Mountains

Keep following the marker until there's a big ice blocking the way.

Use the Prime Ice Construct menu to Remove the blockade.

Keep following the route to advance into the snowstorm, all the way until you find the Statue of the Seven in the area.

Now, the mission will change to: Find the mechanism for the "hidden tracks".

Find and Summon the Mechanism for the "Hidden Tracks"

To find the mechanism for the "hidden tracks" and summon it, follow these steps:

Follow a Seelie next to the Statue of the Seven. If there's no Seelie, keep going up the stairs after passing the Statue. This will lead you to the upper floor.

Remove the ice blocking the way.

Glide down to the left corner to use the elevator.

Continue north following the quest marker. Jump and glide, then climb the tower to reach the console.

Claim the Precious Chest there, then place the Eye of Graeae on the console.

This will summon the train, allowing you to board it.

Aboard the train, you'll be transported to a peculiar world. The quest now changes to: Investigate the strange space.

Investigate the Strange Space

Head to the open office, then interact with the board.

There should be an arrow pointing at a food bowl afterward. Interact with the bowl.

Investigate the Next Room

Use the Snegovik Laboratory Key that you got on the door nearby.

Inside, investigate the Prime Ice on the table to reveal a note.

Read it, then keep shaking the mountain painting on the wall until you reveal a hidden path.

Follow the hidden hall, and you'll get stuck inside the secret room.

Find a Way Out of the Room

Investigate the blue board to see a diagram of Unnamed Potion Formula.

Approach the scale on the table, and try to figure out which item should go on the scale. There's no right answer, as the protagonist will eventually solve the riddle on their own, so just keep trying until you trigger the revelation. Claim the Precious Chest, then leave the room.

Try Opening the Door in Front of the Staircase

Place the cat food in the bowl next to the door, and the cat will drop the bottle, surprising the person inside and making them open the door. Go to the second floor and search for the next clue until you trigger a cutscene.

Head to the Snow-Covered Palace

You’ll arrive at the Pale Crown Palace once the cutscene ends. Go up the stairs and unlock the Teleport Waypoint. Once you reach the waypoint, the To Gaze Upon the Dreaming Pale Crown quest will end, and The Stone Beasts, Like Ghouls Seated mission will start.

item.title: PS5 Gamers: Your Wallet Isn't Ready for August 27
item.description:
PlayStation 5 gamers should be sure to circle Thursday, August 27 on their calendars, as it's set to be a particularly busy day for the platform. Most of the biggest third-party games release on PlayStation 5, with very few exceptions, and Sony also supports the console with exclusive first-party releases. While the console's lack of exclusives compared to its predecessors has been criticized, there's still no denying that the PS5 library is absolutely ridiculous at this point and just keeps getting better.

New PS5 games are released on a regular basis, ensuring that there is always something new to play. Significant new games are released for PS5 every month, with the releases often spread out to avoid competing with one another. Though it's relatively rare, there are times when multiple big new releases all launch on the same day, and that's exactly what's happening on Thursday, August 27.

Brand-New PS5 Game Inspired By Classic PS2-Era Platformers is Getting Great Reviews

A newly released 3D platformer on PlayStation 5 receives rave reviews, with many already comparing it to some of the best PS2 games.

By Mohsen Baqery

New PS5 Games Releasing on August 27

  • Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2
  • Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy
  • Star Wars Zero Company

On Thursday, August 27, PS5 gamers are being treated to Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2 , Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy , and Star Wars Zero Company all on the same day. Needless to say, it's going to be an incredibly busy day for gamers on the platform, especially those that want to play the biggest new releases.

Upcoming Releases

For those unfamiliar with the games, Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 2 is a collection of classic Metal Gear Solid games, with Metal Gear: Ghost Babel , Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots , and Metal Gear Solid: Peace Walker making up the lineup. It marks the first time Metal Gear Solid 4 has been released on something other than PS3, which is something franchise fans have been waiting years for. Master Collection Vol. 2 will retail for $49.99 at launch, which isn't a bad price considering you get three games.

Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy , meanwhile, is an action-adventure game that serves as a prequel to the existing two Plague Tale games. Whereas stealth is a focus in those titles, Resonance focuses on action. The Plague Tale games are known for their impressive visuals, well-written characters, and engaging stories, so here's hoping Resonance is able to keep the franchise's momentum going strong. Those interested in the game should note that Resonance: A Plague Tale Legacy will cost $59.99 at launch.

And finally, there's Star Wars Zero Company , which should go a long way in filling the void left by XCOM . Star Wars Zero Company is a turn-based tactics game that is borrowing a lot from XCOM , including its permadeath and customization, but with a Star Wars skin. What's been shown of Star Wars Zero Company so far has looked incredibly impressive, and it definitely seems like the game will greatly appeal to fans of the genre. If nothing else, it should offer a unique take on a Star Wars video game. Star Wars Zero Company will cost $59.99, so any PS5 gamers looking to buy all three of these at launch is looking at dropping about $170 before tax. Needless to say, August 27 is going to be an expensive day, but at least it seems like the games will be worth it.

item.title: 7 Long Turn-Based RPGs That Take Forever To Complete, Ranked
item.description:
When you boot up a turn-based RPG for the first time, you know you will be seeing that title screen for the next couple of weeks or even months. We want to spend 50 hours exploring the world, perfecting our party's builds, and defeating every optional boss possible. However, the longest turn-based RPGs go well beyond the norm and become a true challenge for those brave enough to embark on a completionist run.

Length isn't always a virtue, but long campaigns fit the vibe of this genre and its combat. Rather than focusing on the main story, let's highlight single-player RPGs at their absolute fullest , ones that throw so much optional content at you that it starts to feel like it never ends. If nothing else, these games give you your money's worth.

A few ground rules:

  • Only single-player console or PC games that can be completed.
  • No mobile/gacha/always online stuff.
  • Only one entry per franchise.
  • No strategy RPGs like Disgaea , Fire Emblem , or Tactics Ogre .
  • HowLongToBeat's Completionist average is used as a reference.

1 Unchained Blades

Hours Of Play On Average: 330 Hours

Average Times:

  • Main Story – 40 Hours
  • Main Story + Extras – 75 Hours
  • Completionist – 330 Hours

Let's kick things off with a turn-based RPG that has been almost entirely forgotten by history. Released on the 3DS and PSP, Unchained Blades plays like a classic first-person dungeon-crawler, albeit with an anime aesthetic akin to something like Etrian Odyssey or the Labyrinth games. While the core campaign falls in line with the standard length for these types of releases, Unchained Blades combines an array of mechanics to create the ultimate completionist nightmare.

9 Great RPGs That Sold Poorly

Not every fantastic game gets the love that it deserves, and these RPGs struggled to meet their commercial goals and became financial flops.

By Ollie Tuscarny

This game features a monster-collecting system, with over 180 species eligible to become followers. Completing the compendium means unchaining every single creature, a process that relies on RNG to even be triggered. The 8 main playable characters have fairly extensive skill trees, making unlocking all the nodes quite an exhausting process.

Naturally, Unchained Blades has quite a bit of post-game content, like optional dungeons and boss battles, and simply grinding levels becomes the ultimate purpose. It just never ends.

I have fond memories of playing Unchained Blades on the PSP, although I never came close to completing it. If you enjoy these sort of dungeon crawlers, you might want to give this one a go.

Hours Of Play On Average: 280 Hours

Average Times:

  • Main Story – 40 Hours
  • Main Story + Extras – 100 Hours
  • Completionist – 280 Hours

Pretty much every Pokemon game takes over your life. The "short" mainline entries still require 20–30 hours just to finish the main campaign, and a Master's journey doesn't end just because they defeat the Elite Four. At the bare minimum, players need to complete the Pokedex and catch every Pokemon, a goal that is easier said than done even when aided by trading.

Pokemon Diamond and Pearl are the longest games in the series by quite a wide margin, and you feel their length on the original hardware. Compared to earlier entries, Diamond and Pearl are quite sluggish, to the point that even opening the menu feels like it takes a bit longer than it should. Battles last a lifetime, and these small moments add up after 100+ hours of gameplay. Completionists also need to unlock the 5-Star Black Card, which involves winning 100 consecutive matches in the Battle Tower.

  • Main Story + Extras – 135 Hours
  • Completionist – 225 Hours

Dense in the way that only CRPGs based on tabletop properties tend to be, Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous combines a steep learning curve and a high barrier for entry with crushing length, even if somebody only aims to finish the campaign.

The central hook involves picking a Mythic Path, and you can only commit to one per playthrough (well, technically, two, as you can swap to an advanced path late in the game). At the end of Act 2, you will need to select from the 6 basic paths, all of which come with new characters, quests, and areas.   • Main Story + Extras – 115 Hours

However, Persona 5 ultimately comes out as the longer game for a couple of reasons.

Royal introduces quite a few quality-of-life adjustments that reduce the grind, busy work, and help speed things up. Players fly through the months far quicker in the updated version, and the process to complete the Persona compendium simply takes longer than the original game. A single playthrough is already an undertaking, but you need to at least play New Game+ to make different choices than in the first run, complete the Confidant routes, spark new romances, and to fuse the ultimate Persona.

Hours Of Play On Average: 165 Hours

Average Times:

  • Main Story + Extras – 80 Hours
  • Completionist – 145 Hours

Let's end things with maybe the most popular turn-based RPG series of all time: Final Fantasy . Square Enix's franchise features almost exclusively long games, but Final Fantasy 10 has completionist expectations that far exceed every other entry. The main story should already require around 50 hours, and then you'll have to dive into the endless post-game content.

To unlock the Nemesis boss in the Monster Arena and get an associated trophy, players need to capture 10 of every monster, and FF10 has 102 of them. They will need to unlock every character's Celestial Weapon and max out their Sphere Grid, both of which can be grinds. Those are far from the only things that must be done, and the PS2 version didn't come with the 4x speed boost of the dual-pack remaster.

item.title: How to Get Optical Camo in Ghost Recon Breakpoint
item.description:
Optical Camo was added to Ghost Recon Breakpoint as part of the Operation Motherland update. To get it, players need to play Operation Motherland's Conquest mode and progress enough through the storyline until they reach their first major mission. Unlocking the Optical Camo in Breakpoint should take about half an hour or so, depending on how quickly players can sabotage the Bodarks' operation and storm one of their bases in southern Auroa.

Best Mods for Ghost Recon Breakpoint

Here are some of the best mods to use if you want to spice up your Ghost Recon Breakpoint experience.

By Marc Santos

Where to Find the Optical Camo in Ghost Recon Breakpoint

First, you'll need to swap over to Conquest mode by opening your map and selecting the button on the lower-right side of your screen . You can freely swap between the main campaign and Conquest at any time, and your progress between the two modes will be tracked and saved separately, which means you won't have to worry about losing any progress.

Once you start Conquest mode, complete the prologue, then complete at least two Destabilization missions against Bodark . After finishing those missions, you'll get another mission that will send you to an enemy outpost in Eternity . Head to the marked objective, and once you reach the facility, look for a tech crate on the first floor of the main building. Open it to get the Optical Camo device.

Bodark's forces are pretty tough, so make sure you bring the best gear you got.

How to Use Optical Camo in Ghost Recon Breakpoint

After getting the Optical Camo device, you can press the U key/D-Pad Left to activate it . The Optical Camo's battery will slowly drain for as long as it's active, and it'll drain even faster if you're moving (and even more so if you're performing more extreme actions like sprinting, vaulting, or shooting).

By default, Optical Camo will only recharge during daytime , so you'll want to use it sparingly during night raids. Later on, you can purchase an upgrade that lets your Optical Camo device recharge even during nighttime.

Without any upgrades, the Optical Camo is best used the same way as the Prone Camo feature. If you're at risk of getting seen (such as when you're lining up a sniper rifle shot), go invisible, then stay perfectly still until enemies pass you.

How to Upgrade Optical Camo

To upgrade your Optical Camo, you need to collect Camo Points , which you can collect by opening crates throughout Auroa . Check points of interest on your map to see if they have Camo Point crates inside them, and if they do, you can easily find where they are by using your drone and looking for a circular symbol somewhere on the map.

The best places to get tons of Camo Points at once are Behemoth Defense Areas . These locations have 1000 Camo Points up for grabs, and while they are always guarded by a Behemoth drone the first time you visit them, you don't have to destroy them to get the Camo Points. Just sneak past the Behemoth, grab the Camo Points from the crate inside the defense area, then fast back to the safety of the nearest Bivouac.

You can find the various Optical Camo upgrades by going to the Loadout screen. The cloak will fizzle out very quickly if you anything except stand perfectly still, so make sure to upgrade it as often as you can.

Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Breakpoint
